idiom_name: generic getOrLoad<K, V>() over a Map of { value, expiresAt, inflight }
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a type contract to the same runtime shape: a Map<string, CacheEntry<T>> with an explicit miss protocol and a generic getOrLoad(key, load) helper that awaits the loader on a miss and stores { value, expiresAt }, with the in-flight promise kept under the same key so concurrent misses share one load. The runtime provides only Map, so TTL, eviction and invalidation are hand-written exactly as in JavaScript; the type parameters only make the key/value contract explicit. For a shared cache the helper wraps a client such as ioredis and the payload type becomes a serialization boundary that should be validated rather than trusted.
pitfalls: JSON round-trips do not carry types: a value read from a remote cache must be validated at the boundary, because an as-cast drops unknown and the type error surfaces far from the cache.
A key built inconsistently (object identity, casing, missing namespace) misses forever; normalize keys in one place.
Serverless and short-lived processes are per instance, so an in-process Map is best-effort - use Redis when multiple instances must agree.

variants.name: lru-cache with typed fetch()
variants.idiom_name: new LRUCache<string, Entity>({ max, ttl }).fetch(key, loader)
variants.implementation_notes: The typed wrapper over the popular library: new LRUCache<string, Entity>({ max, ttl }) bounds the store and fetch(key, loader) implements read-with-populate, deduplicating concurrent fetches and skipping the insert when the entry was deleted, evicted or overwritten while the loader ran. delete(key) after the store commit is the invalidation step, and the generic parameters keep the loader and the consumer honest about the value type; the package works unchanged in Node and in browsers.
pitfalls: fetch() does not store rejections, which is correct but turns a failing source into repeated load attempts - add a short negative cache when the source is down.
ttl applies from insertion; sliding-window or stale-while-revalidate behaviour must be chosen explicitly, and it changes what a cache hit means.
Type parameters are erased at runtime: values from a remote store still need validation, and an evicted in-flight fetch is not inserted.
